record.original_question: If G is a pro-Lie group and G0 is its identity component, must the quotient group G/G0 be complete? Equivalently in the paper's discussion, is G/G0 always prodiscrete?

evidence.quote: The answer to following question is unknown: Question 2. Let G be a pro-Lie group with identity component G0. Is G/G0 complete (and therefore prodiscrete)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A topological group G is called a pro-Lie group if it is isomorphic (as a topological group) to a closed subgroup of a Cartesian product of finite-dimensional real Lie groups; equivalently, G is complete, Hausdorff, and the filter basis of closed normal subgroups N such that G/N is a finite-dimensional Lie group converges to the identity. A topological group is called prodiscrete if it is isomorphic to a closed subgroup of a Cartesian product of discrete groups, equivalently if it is complete and the closed normal subgroups with discrete quotient form a neighborhood basis of the identity.

Let G be a pro-Lie group, and let G_0 denote its identity component (the connected component of the identity element). The quotient G/G_0 is a Hausdorff topological group whose underlying topological space is totally disconnected.

Question: Must G/G_0 be complete (equivalently, must G/G_0 be a prodiscrete topological group) for every pro-Lie group G?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as Question 2 in the 2015 Hofmann–Morris survey on pro-Lie groups and is explicitly stated as unknown there. A 2018 paper by Dahmen and Hofmann ("On the Component Factor Group G/G_0 of a Pro-Lie Group G", arXiv:1812.04838) establishes the result in the almost-connected case, proving that if every Lie quotient G/N has finitely many components then G/G_0 is compact (in particular complete). The general question for arbitrary pro-Lie groups does not appear to be resolved in subsequent surveys, so it is best classified as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Pro-Lie Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Question 2. Let G be a pro-Lie group with identity component G_0. Is G/G_0 complete (and therefore prodiscrete)?
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly listed as an unknown open problem in the survey.

status_evidence.title: On the Component Factor Group G/G_0 of a Pro-Lie Group G
status_evidence.snippet: A pro-Lie group G is almost connected if each of its Lie group quotients G/N has finitely many connected components.
status_evidence.claim: Resolves the almost-connected case, showing G/G_0 is compact (hence complete) under that hypothesis, but not the general question.
